html:
"Bosporian Kingdom" is the map's spelling, from 1 to 200 CE, for the Bosporan Kingdom on the Strait of Kerch in the centuries when it was a client of Rome. It was the longest-lasting of Rome's client kingdoms.

After Mithridates VI died at Panticapaeum in 63 BCE, Rome let a series of kings rule the strait as long as they stayed loyal. From the early first century CE a dynasty whose kings took the Roman names Tiberius Julius ruled for about three hundred years, and their coins carried the emperor's portrait. Under Nero, from 63 to 68 CE, the kingdom was briefly made part of a Roman province before being restored.

The first and second centuries CE were a new golden age. The kingdom hosted Roman troops and ships, sold grain to Roman armies, and fought off the Sarmatian and Alan nomads around it. At the end of the 100s CE King Sauromates II beat the Scythians and took the whole of Crimea.

From the 250s the Goths used Bosporan ships to raid Asia Minor. The kingdom faded in the 300s, and the arrival of the Huns around 370 is usually taken as its end, though the strait was later held by the Byzantines.
